newsitem.title: USA: Chevron settles gender discrimination suit.
newsitem.headline: Chevron settles gender discrimination suit.

text.p: Chevron Corp said on Wednesday its unit Chevron Information Technology Co has settled a multi-million dollar gender discrimination class action lawsuit.

The case involved 777 current and former CITC female employees who had sued the San Ramon-based unit of Chevron claiming gender discrimination. The agreement is subject to approval by the San Francisco Superior Court.

Under the settlement, class members may elect an expedited claims procedure by filing a wage claim and receiving a payment based upon their salary level and years of service or have wage claims decided by a neutral arbitrator.

If all class members were to submit an expedited claim, the total cost to the company for wage claims would be $7.42 million, including interest. Depending on the number of those who file for arbitration, and the outcome of that arbitration, the eventual cost to the company may be higher.

Chevron said claims for emotional distress may also be filed and, depending on severity, class members may recover $5,000, $20,000 or $50,000. Most women who file successful emotional distress claims will be compensated at $5,000. Awards for $5,000 may be prorated if the total amount of $5,000 awards exceed a cap of $1 million.
The $20,000 and $50,000 awards are not subject to proration and may require medical documentation and an arbitration hearing.
CITC has agreed to contribute $150,000 to not-for-profit women's support organizations, while attorneys representing the women will contribute a total of $50,000.
The company said it has also agreed to put in place a variety of new programs to enhance diversity efforts and create a more supportive environment for employees.

The class action suit was filed on August 19, 1992, alleging sex discrimination and sexual harassment. In February 1994 the court granted class certification of the sex discrimination claims but denied certification of the sexual harassment claims. Individual claims of sexual harassment were settled in February 1995.
